# Daily seismic velocity change (dv/v) between station pairs, from ambient noise

## Terms

Derived from the region's waveforms; tokens carry the licence the region states (INGV's Italian networks: CC BY 4.0, cite the network DOI).

## Cite

- INGV Seismological Data Centre (2006). Rete Sismica Nazionale (RSN). doi:10.13127/SD/X0FXNH7QFY
- Shapiro, N. M., Campillo, M. (2004). Emergence of broadband Rayleigh waves from correlations of the ambient seismic noise. GRL 31, L07614.
- Sens-Schönfelder, C., Wegler, U. (2006). Passive image interferometry and seasonal variations of seismic velocities at Merapi Volcano. GRL 33, L21302.
- Hobiger, M., Wegler, U., Shiomi, K., Nakahara, H. (2012). Coseismic and postseismic velocity changes detected by passive image interferometry. JGR 117, B09313.
- Weaver, R. L., Hadziioannou, C., Larose, E., Campillo, M. (2011). On the precision of noise correlation interferometry. GJI 185, 1393-1404.
- Zhan, Z., Tsai, V. C., Clayton, R. W. (2013). Spurious velocity changes caused by temporal variations in ambient noise frequency content. GJI 194, 1574-1581.

## Access

The same cached 1 Hz LH waveforms as seismic_noise_power (nothing new is downloaded). Daily correlations are computed on the GPU and cached per month under data/cache/velocity/, keyed by the raw files and the settings.

## From the source to the token

| Token slot | Comes from |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `observation` |
| `lat, lon` | the midpoint of the two stations |
| `depth_km` | minus the two stations' mean elevation / 1000 |
| `time` | midnight UTC starting the last day of the stack |
| `value` | dvv (corrected), dvv_raw, coherence |
| `uncertainty` | Weaver et al. (2011) σ, combined over the component pairs |
| `qualifiers` | station_a, station_b, stack_days, reference |
| `resolution` | half the station distance, and the stack's days |

## Uncertainty

From the coherence of each component's stretch (Weaver et al. 2011), combined as 1/sqrt(Σ 1/σ²). It assumes the nine components are independent, which they are not quite: real day-to-day scatter is larger (in the lesson).

## Known issues

- 1 Hz data: the band is 0.1-0.45 Hz, below the 0.5-1 Hz where published studies saw the clearest coseismic drops in central Italy.
- The reference is the region's quiet period; dv/v is relative to it and means nothing across regions.
- The correction is fitted on the reference period only; a drift that starts after it (a new sensor, a new site) stays in dvv.
- Stacks read only past days, so a step shows up spread over the stack.
- Pairs farther apart than max_pair_km (80 km) are not correlated.
